title: The Role of Science Education in Developing 21st-Century Competencies, Specifically Critical Thinking Skills
abstract: Critical Students’ critical thinking skills in science learning remain underdeveloped due to teacher-centered instructional practices and limited engagement in meaningful scientific activities. In addition, the integration of science process skills and scientific literacy has not been systematically implemented, resulting in suboptimal student participation. This study aims to analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of integrating science process skills and scientific literacy in enhancing students’ critical thinking abilities. This research employed a systematic literature review involving 30 reputable scholarly articles as the unit of analysis. Data were collected through documentation techniques from scientific databases using an analysis sheet based on critical thinking indicators. The data were analyzed using content analysis to identify patterns of findings, methodological trends, and consistency across studies. The results indicate that science learning integrating inquiry, problem-solving, experimentation, and discussion effectively promotes students’ analytical, evaluative, and reflective thinking skills. title: Bilingual Picture Guessing Cards on Science Material to Improve Positive Relationships for Third-Grade Inclusive Elementary Students
abstract: Social interaction between deaf students and regular students in inclusive classrooms tends to be limited, which affects the participation of deaf students in learning activities. This condition is also influenced by the use of learning media that have not fully accommodated the learning needs of students with special needs and have not optimally supported inclusive communication in the classroom. This study aims to analyze learning needs, develop, and evaluate the feasibility of a bilingual guessing picture card media in science learning to strengthen the positive relationship among inclusive third-grade elementary students. This study employed a research and development approach using the ADDIE model, which consists of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation stages. The subject of this study was the bilingual guessing picture card media, while the research objects included content validity and user responses to the developed media. The study involved one teacher and 20 third-grade students consisting of regular students and deaf students. title: Interactive Multimedia Based on the Think Pair Share Cooperative Model Effectively Improves Mathematical Competence
abstract: The mathematics learning process in educational institutions is still dominated by the use of student worksheets without the support of varied and interactive learning media. This condition affects students’ low competence in understanding whole number concepts. This study aims to analyze the design, assess the feasibility, and evaluate the effectiveness of interactive multimedia based on the cooperative learning model Think Pair Share (TPS) to enhance students’ mathematics competence. This is a research and development (R&D) study employing the ADDIE model. The research subjects involved four experts (instructional design expert, content expert, media expert, and instructional development expert) and 35 fifth-grade students as trial participants. Data were collected using validation questionnaires, observations, and learning outcome tests. The data were analyzed using descriptive quantitative techniques for validation and product trials, and an inferential one-sample t-test to measure media effectiveness. The results showed that the interactive multimedia was highly feasible, with validation scores from all experts exceeding 90%. The effectiveness test indicated that the calculate

title: PKM Instruction Based on Contextual Teaching and Learning to Enhance Elementary School Students’ Empathy Toward Their Peers
abstract: The low level of empathy among elementary school students, as reflected in their lack of concern for peers in daily interactions, combined with a teaching approach that remains teacher-centered, has not yet optimally developed students’ affective aspects. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of Moral Citizenship Education (PKM) instruction based on Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL) in enhancing students’ empathy. The subjects of this study were all 24 first-grade students, using a pre-experimental one-shot case study design. Data were collected using a validated empathy attitude scale and observation sheets, then analyzed using descriptive and inferential techniques. The results of the study indicate that the implementation of Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL)-based instruction significantly enhances students’ empathy, as evidenced by behavioral changes toward greater caring, the ability to understand peers’ feelings, and more positive social interactions. These findings are supported by observational data showing increased social sensitivity and student engagement in the learning process. title: Literature Review: The Influence of Digital-Based Learning Media on Civics Learning in Elementary Schools
abstract: With the development of technology and the transformation of education into a new paradigm, there have been adjustments in the use of Civic Education learning media at the elementary school level. This study aims to analyze digital learning media and their impact on Citizenship Education (PKN) learning in elementary schools within the context of the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum. The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with a PRISMA approach, which includes the stages of identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion. Data sources were obtained from several databases such as Google Scholar, Eric, ScienceDirect, and Scopus with articles published from 2022 to 2025. From a total of 13,030 articles, 18 relevant articles were obtained and analyzed in depth. Data analysis techniques in this study included qualitative and quantitative descriptive approaches for comprehensive results. The research findings indicate that there are six main categories of digital learning media used: dynamic audio-visual media, static visual media, interactive media, game-based media, digital physical device-based media, and interactive digital book media. title: Educational Digital Comics to Improve Reading Comprehension Skills Among Fourth-Grade Elementary School Students
abstract: Elementary students’ reading comprehension remains low, partly due to the limited availability of engaging and developmentally appropriate learning media. This study aims to develop, test the feasibility, practicality, and effectiveness of educational digital comics in improving students’ reading comprehension skills. This is a research and development (R&D) study using the ADDIE model. The research subjects consist of two subject matter experts, one media expert, one instructional design expert, one fourth-grade teacher, and 15 fourth-grade students as test participants. Data were collected through questionnaires, tests, and documentation using expert validation sheets, teacher and student response questionnaires, and multiple-choice reading comprehension tests. The data were analyzed using descriptive qualitative and quantitative methods to assess the feasibility, practicality, and effectiveness of the media. The research results indicate that the developed educational digital comics are highly suitable, as assessed by subject matter experts, media experts, and instructional design experts. Feedback from teachers and students indicates that the medium is highly practical and easy

title: The Effectiveness of the Guided Inquiry Learning Model Assisted by the Bumibutuhaksi Account on Students’ Literacy Regarding Climate Change Disaster Mitigation
abstract: Students’ low literacy regarding climate change disaster mitigation indicates that geography learning has not fully developed ecological awareness and preparedness toward global environmental challenges. In addition, the utilization of social media as a contextual learning resource remains suboptimal, resulting in theoretical and less meaningful learning experiences. This study aims to analyze and examine the effectiveness of a guided inquiry learning model supported by an educational social media account in improving students’ climate change disaster mitigation literacy. The research employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design involving 64 students as research subjects. Data were collected through literacy tests, observation sheets, and attitude questionnaires, and analyzed using N-Gain analysis and inferential statistical testing. The findings reveal that the implementation of the guided inquiry model assisted by social media significantly enhances students’ literacy across cognitive, skill, and attitudinal dimensions. title: The Effect of the Catur Pramana Learning Cycle Method Using Augmented Reality Media on the Learning Outcomes of Grade 5 Primary School Students
abstract: The low student ability in understanding classroom learning materials indicates persistent problems in the learning process. This condition is influenced by the use of less varied instructional media, which tends to rely solely on videos from the internet without being supported by methods that strengthen students’ conceptual understanding. This study aims to analyze the effect of the Catur Pramana learning cycle method assisted by Augmented Reality media on elementary students’ science (IPAS) learning outcomes. This study employed a quasi-experimental design with a non-equivalent post-test only control group design. The research subjects consisted of 38 fifth-grade students who were divided into an experimental group and a control group through random sampling techniques. Data were collected using a multiple-choice test as the research instrument. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive quantitative analysis followed by an independent t-test to examine the research hypothesis. title: Evaluation Study of Inclusive Education at the Elementary School Level at Hainan School
abstract: The implementation of inclusive education in regular elementary schools still faces various challenges in providing appropriate educational services for students with special needs. Limitations in curriculum adaptation, teacher competence, and instructional strategies often hinder the realization of inclusive learning environments that accommodate diverse student needs. This study aims to evaluate and analyze the implementation of inclusive education at the elementary school level using the CIPP evaluation model, which includes context, input, process, and product components. This research employed a qualitative approach involving 12 research subjects consisting of school principals, classroom teachers, special assistant teachers, and students. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation using observation guidelines, interview protocols, and documentation sheets as research instruments. The data were analyzed using qualitative data analysis techniques through the stages of data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. title: The Effect of Ethnomathematics-Based Problem-Based Learning Model on the Numeracy Literacy Skills of Fifth Grade Elementary School Students in Cluster 2
abstract: Ideally, learning should be implemented to support the achievement of competencies and foster student literacy, using learning models, media, and other educational tools that are tailored to the learning needs. However, in practice, many teachers are still found to use conventional learning models, where students only acquire knowledge that is directly transmitted by their teacher. This results in students lacking a good understanding of mathematical problem-solving concepts, making it difficult for them to grasp arithmetic concepts. This research aims to analyze the influence of the Ethnomathematics-based Problem Based Learning model on Numeracy Literacy abilities. This type of research is experimental research. This research uses a form of research (quasi experimental). The quasi- experimental design used was a non-equivalent post-test only control group design. The population of this study was all class V of SD Gugus 2, totaling 148 students. The sampling technique uses random sampling. title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy, External Support, and Teaching Competence Development among Kindergarten Teachers: Evidence from Guizhou Province
abstract: This study investigates the relationships among artificial intelligence (AI) literacy, external support, teaching efficacy, and teaching competence development among kindergarten teachers in underdeveloped regions of China. Data were collected from 236 teachers across five public kindergartens in Xingyi City, Guizhou Province. Using quantitative research methods, including multiple regression and mediation analysis, the study examined how teachers' technological cognition, instructional integration ability, and external support affect their teaching competence, and whether teaching efficacy mediates these relationships. title: The Guided Inquiry Learning Model Assisted by Tri Hita Karana Learning Videos on Students’ Learning Activeness and IPAS Learning Outcomes of Fourth-Grade Elementary School Students
abstract: This research is motivated by the low learning activity and learning outcomes of students in science, which are suspected to be influenced by the use of learning models that are not optimal in actively involving students. This study aims to analyze and test the effect of the guided inquiry learning model assisted by Tri Hita Karana-based learning videos on students' learning activity and learning outcomes in science. This study uses a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental research type and a posttest control group design. The research subjects consisted of elementary school students who were divided into an experimental group and a control group selected through a random sampling technique. Data on learning activity were collected through observation sheets, while data on science learning outcomes were obtained through a validated multiple-choice test. Data analysis was carried out using multivariate analysis techniques to test the effects partially and simultaneously. The results showed that there were significant differences in learning activity and science learning outcomes between students who participated in learning with the guided inquiry model assisted by Tri Hita

title: Values and Character Education in the 21st Century Family
abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technology has transformed social interaction patterns and created new challenges in shaping children’s values and character. Unfiltered exposure to digital information may negatively influence behavior, attitudes, and moral development if it is not balanced by strong value education within the family. This study aims to analyze and explore the strategic role of families in values and character education for children in the 21st-century digital era. The research employed a qualitative approach using a literature review method, examining scholarly sources including academic books, reputable journal articles, and educational policy documents. Data were collected through documentation techniques and analyzed using thematic analysis to identify patterns of family roles in character formation. The findings reveal that families function as primary socialization agents through parental role modeling, the implementation of positive discipline, open and supportive communication, reinforcement of positive behavior, and children’s involvement in family decision-making processes. title: Evaluating Students’ Artificial Intelligence Literacy: Development of an Assessment Instrument Based on Experiential Learning Elements
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) literacy has become an essential competency for students in responding to rapid digital transformation across various fields. However, the limited availability of valid and reliable assessment instruments constrains the comprehensive evaluation of students’ AI literacy levels. This study aims to analyze, develop, and validate an AI literacy assessment instrument based on experiential learning elements and a deep learning approach. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) design consisting of needs analysis, instrument design, development, validation testing, and data analysis stages. The research involved 500 students selected through multistage sampling techniques. Data were collected using an AI literacy questionnaire designed to measure three main components: knowledge, affective attitudes, and critical thinking skills, which are integrated with global competencies required in the 21st century. Construct validity was examined using factor analysis, while reliability was assessed through internal consistency analysis. title: The Quantum Learning Model Assisted by Puzzle Game Media on the Scientific Attitudes and Science Learning Outcomes of Fifth Grade Students
abstract: This research is motivated by the low scientific attitudes and science learning outcomes of students, which are thought to be influenced by the use of learning models that lack variety and are unable to encourage active student involvement. This study aims to examine the effect of the Quantum learning model assisted by puzzle games on the scientific attitudes and science learning outcomes of elementary school students. This study used an experimental research type with a post-test only control group design. The research subjects consisted of two groups of students divided into an experimental group and a control group. Data on scientific attitudes were collected through questionnaires, while data on science learning outcomes were obtained through tests. The instruments used ensured that they had gone through a validation process for measurement feasibility. Data analysis was conducted using multivariate analysis techniques. The results showed that there were significant differences in scientific attitudes and science learning outcomes between students who participated in learning with the Quantum model assisted by puzzle media and students who participated in conventional learning.

title: Analysis of Fourth-Grade Students' Science Process Skills: A Comparative Descriptive Quantitative Study Between Sekolah Penggerak and Non-Sekolah Penggerak
abstract: The low mastery of science process skills among elementary school students poses a challenge in science education. This study aims to analyze the differences in science process skills among fourth-grade students in Sekolah Penggerak and Bukan Sekolah Penggerak. This research employs a quantitative descriptive method, with data collected through a science process skills test covering five key aspects: observing, classifying, predicting, concluding, and communicating. The study sample consists of 37 fourth-grade students selected using a convenience sampling technique. The collected data were analyzed descriptively using percentages and categorized based on science process skills achievement levels. The findings reveal that students in Sekolah Penggerak achieved an average science process skills attainment of 72% (high category), whereas students in Bukan Sekolah Penggerak attained 64% (moderate category). Students in Sekolah Penggerak excelled in predicting and concluding aspects, while those in Bukan Sekolah Penggerak faced difficulties across all aspects of science process skills. title: Evaluation of Laboratory Facilities and Infrastructure in Vocational High Schools: A Case Study of the Beauty and Hairdressing Program
abstract: The inadequate fulfillment of laboratory facilities and infrastructure standards in vocational secondary schools remains a critical challenge in ensuring the quality of practice-based learning aligned with professional competency demands. The mismatch between existing facilities and national standards may hinder student’s technical skill development and limit the effective implementation of occupational safety and health principles during practical learning activities. This study aimed to analyze and evaluate the gaps in laboratory facilities and infrastructure within the skin and hair beauty expertise program based on established standards. The research employed a quantitative approach using a program evaluation design with a discrepancy model. The participants consisted of 9 teachers and 100 students who utilized laboratory practice facilities. Data were collected through questionnaires, observations, interviews, and documentation, and were analyzed using descriptive statistical techniques. The findings revealed that the fulfillment level of laboratory facilities and infrastructure was categorized as moderate, with notable gaps in the completeness of practice equipment, availabil

title: Cross-Functional Skills Analysis of Vocational High School Students to Face Industrial Changes in Lubuklinggau
abstract: Rapid changes in the industrial sector require vocational education graduates to possess cross-functional skills that enable them to adapt to complex and dynamic workplace situations. However, several studies indicate that these skills have not yet been optimally developed among vocational high school students, highlighting the need for a comprehensive analysis of students’ cross-functional skill profiles. This study aims to analyze and explore the level of cross-functional skills of vocational high school students based on school level, skill aspects, and areas of specialization. This research employed a quantitative approach involving 192 students selected from a population of 379 students using proportionate cluster random sampling based on the Isaac and Michael table with a 5% error rate. Data were collected using a cross-functional skills questionnaire with a 4-point Likert scale covering five main aspects: social skills, system skills, complex problem solving, resource management skills, and technical skills. The data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. The findings reveal that students’ cross-functional skills are generally categorized as good, with m

title: Analysis of Elementary School Science Content and Scientific Attitudes in Satua Bali for Culturally Responsive Learning
abstract: Culture-integrated learning remains suboptimal, partly due to limited understanding of Balinese satua content, which is rich in science concepts and scientific attitudes. In fact, elementary science learning that integrates local wisdom values can provide meaningful and contextual learning experiences for students. This study aims to analyze elementary science content and scientific attitudes in three Balinese satua: Angsa teken Kerkuak, I Alu teken I Kedis Puuh, and I Berit Kuning, to support culturally responsive teaching. This research employs a literature review approach using the library research method. Data were collected through document analysis from books, journal articles, previous studies, and relevant digital sources, using a journal note-taking instrument. Data validity was ensured through peer debriefing with supervisors and colleagues, while data analysis was conducted using narrative analysis. The findings indicate that the three Balinese satua contain science content relevant to elementary education, including ecosystems, habitats, adaptation of living organisms, plant body parts, types of animal food, growth and development, reproductive systems, and sound. title: Interactive Flashcard Media with Images Containing Indonesian Cultural Heritage Based on Canva to Improve Beginning Reading Skills and Motivation in Grade 1 Elementary School Students
abstract: The low level of beginning reading skills among elementary school students is often caused by the use of learning media that are less engaging and have not integrated cultural elements into the learning process. In addition, interactive and contextual learning media are still limited, so they are less able to increase students’ learning motivation at the early reading stage. This study aims to develop and evaluate the feasibility of interactive flashcard media with images containing Indonesian cultural heritage based on Canva in improving beginning reading skills and motivation of first-grade elementary school students. This study used the Research and Development (R&D) method with the 4D development model (define, design, develop, disseminate). The research subjects consisted of 60 first-grade elementary school students. Data collection techniques were carried out through observation, interviews, and questionnaires, while data analysis used quantitative descriptive analysis with score conversion into qualitative categories. The results showed that the interactive flashcard media obtained an average expert validation score of 3.33 with a very feasible category, and the field trial

title: STEM Implementation and Its Challenges in Inclusive Elementary Schools
abstract: The STEM approach is widely recognized as an effective framework for developing students’ critical thinking, problem-solving, and creativity skills required in twenty-first-century learning. However, the implementation of STEM in inclusive elementary classrooms still faces challenges that may hinder effective learning participation for all students, including those with special educational needs. This study aims to analyze and explore the implementation of STEM and identify factors contributing to teachers’ difficulties in implementing STEM-based learning in inclusive classrooms. This research employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive design. The participants consisted of four teachers (three classroom teachers and one special education teacher) and twelve students, including ten regular students and two deaf students. Data were collected through observations, in-depth interviews, and document analysis using observation guidelines, interview protocols, and document analysis sheets. title: Interactive Multimedia of Local Wisdom of Mekotek Tradition Based on Global Diversity in Indonesian Cultural Heritage Material
abstract: This study was motivated by the lack of use of varied and innovative media and learning resources by teachers in the learning process, which resulted in monotonous learning and had an impact on the low learning outcomes of students. This study aims to: (1) design and develop interactive multimedia based on the local wisdom of the Mekotek tradition, (2) analyse the feasibility of interactive multimedia in terms of content, instructional design, media, and user response, and (3) test the effectiveness of the multimedia in improving student learning outcomes. This study employs a research and development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model. The test subjects consist of 17 students. Data collection techniques include expert validation questionnaires, user trial surveys, and learning outcome tests. Data analysis is conducted using descriptive quantitative methods and a paired sample t-test. title: Early Grade STEM Learning in Elementary Schools in Buleleng District Reviewed from Rural and Urban Areas
abstract: Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM)-based learning is a strategic approach to equipping elementary school students with 21st-century skills such as critical thinking, collaboration, creativity, and problem-solving. However, its implementation still faces disparities among educational settings, particularly concerning teacher readiness, resource availability, and contextual learning environments. This study aims to analyze the implementation of STEM learning in lower-grade elementary classrooms by comparing its characteristics across rural and urban educational contexts. The research employed a qualitative descriptive design involving four lower-grade teachers from two schools representing both contexts. Data were collected through classroom observations, in-depth interviews, and document studies, then analyzed using the interactive model of Miles and Huberman to identify implementation patterns, supporting factors, and barriers. The results revealed that STEM learning in rural settings tends to be simpler and more contextual, utilizing natural learning resources, whereas urban schools apply more varied and exploratory approaches supported by adequate facilities

title: Learning Fable Texts through Retelling Strategies in Developing Reading Culture for Elementary School Students
abstract: Reading interest and reading culture are fundamental foundations for strengthening literacy from an early age in elementary school. However, students’ reading habits remain low due to learning methods that are less engaging and fail to actively involve them in the process. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of the retelling strategy in teaching fable texts as an effort to develop the reading culture of elementary school students. The study employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design involving fourth-grade students. Research instruments included pre-test and post-test assessments, a reading culture questionnaire, and observation sheets documenting students’ activities during the learning process. The findings revealed an improvement in students’ reading skills and comprehension of fable texts after the implementation of the retelling strategy. The activity of retelling not only reinforced students’ understanding of the moral messages and meanings within fables but also fostered emotional engagement, enriched imagination, and cultivated sustainable reading habits. title: The Cooperative Learning Model Type Student Teams Achievement Divisions (STAD) Assisted by Wordwall Media on Mathematics Learning Outcomes
abstract: Low mathematics learning outcomes among elementary school students are often caused by limited variation in learning models and the use of less engaging media. This study aims to develop and examine the effect of the cooperative learning model Student Teams Achievement Divisions (STAD) assisted by Wordwall media on students’ mathematics learning outcomes. This study employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design, specifically a non-equivalent control group design. The population consisted of 150 fourth-grade students, and the sample was selected using cluster random sampling, involving students from two schools. Data were collected using tests as the primary instrument and analyzed through descriptive and inferential methods to assess differences in learning outcomes between the experimental and control groups. The results indicate that implementing STAD combined with Wordwall media significantly improves students’ mathematics learning outcomes compared to conventional learning. The study concludes that integrating cooperative learning with interactive digital media can enhance motivation, engagement, and conceptual understanding, providing an innovative solution

title: Empowering Teacher Leaders: Implementing Differentiated Instruction in Primary School English Classes with the Merdeka Curriculum
abstract: This study examines the role of motivational teachers in implementing differentiated learning in the Merdeka Curriculum in elementary school English classes as a strategy to accommodate the diverse learning needs of students. However, its implementation still faces challenges in the form of limited time, resources, and inadequate teacher training. This study aims to investigate how teacher leaders navigate these challenges and apply differentiated teaching strategies in their classrooms. This study employs a qualitative descriptive approach with a phenomenological focus, aiming to capture the lived experiences of teacher leaders in a primary school. Data collection methods include semi-structured interviews, classroom observations, document analysis, and questionnaires. The data were analyzed using Miles and Huberman's interactive model, which includes data reduction, display, conclusion drawing, and triangulation to ensure validity. The results indicate that while teacher leaders demonstrate a strong understanding of differentiated instruction, they face significant challenges in its implementation, including a lack of time, inadequate resources, and limited technological support.

title: Problem-Based Learning (PBL) E-Module for Fourth Grade IPAS Subject Matter
abstract: Low student motivation and learning outcomes in IPAS learning are major challenges in achieving meaningful learning objectives. This condition indicates the need for the development of interactive and contextual teaching media to increase student engagement in the learning process. This study aims to analyze the development process, test the validity, and evaluate the effectiveness of problem-based learning e-modules in improving student learning outcomes in IPAS subjects. This study is a research and development (R&D) study using the ADDIE model, which includes the stages of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. The research subjects include learning content experts, learning design experts, and learning media experts, while the test subjects consist of 3 students (individual test), 9 students (small group test), and 20 students (field test). Data were collected through interviews, documentation, validation questionnaires, and learning outcome tests using validated instruments. Data analysis techniques included qualitative descriptive analysis, quantitative descriptive analysis, and inferential t-test statistics. The research results indicate that the e-mo

title: The Impact of the Make a Match Type Cooperative Learning Model E-Module on Fostering Students’ Love for the Homeland
abstract: Students' limited knowledge about Indonesia leads to a lack of patriotism. This issue is exacerbated by the lack of innovative teaching methods that promote active and engaging learning. In response, a study was conducted to assess the impact of the Make a Match type Cooperative learning model, supported by e-modules, on fostering patriotism in the Pancasila Education subject. The study used a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design, specifically a non-equivalent post-test only control group design. The population included all fifth-grade students from SD, totaling 135 students. A cluster random sampling technique was applied, resulting in a sample of 40 students 20 from SD as the experimental group and 20 from SD as the control group. Data on patriotism attitudes were collected through a non-test method using a questionnaire, which was then analyzed using inferential statistics (independent sample t-test). The analysis revealed a significant effect of the Make a Match type Cooperative learning model with e-modules on improving the students' patriotism in Pancasila Education. title: Exploration of Students' Autonomous Learning Motivation in Educational Technology Environments
abstract: The main problem in student independent learning is low intrinsic motivation, which is often hampered by educational platform designs that are not sufficiently supportive. In addition, the influence of cultural factors and learning support mechanisms on the quality of independent learning is not yet fully understood. This study aims to analyze the factors that influence students' self-directed learning motivation, evaluate the role of educational technology platform design, and synthesize the relationship between motivation types and learning quality with reference to the Self-Determination Theory (SDT) framework. This study uses a mixed method with a sequential explanatory design. The quantitative subjects consisted of 400 students who used Learning Management Systems, mobile learning applications, and AI-based tutor systems, while 30 students were involved in the qualitative stage through semi-structured interviews and platform log analysis. Data were collected through SDT-based questionnaires, interview guidelines, and digital activity logs. Analysis was conducted using Pearson's correlation test, regression, and qualitative thematic analysis to reinforce the findings. The resul

title: Model Influence Problem-Based Learning by Animated Videos Based on Local Wisdom on Learning Motivation and Mathematics Learning Outcomes
abstract: Low levels of motivation and learning outcomes in mathematics remain a major issue in elementary education. Conventional learning approaches tend to provide limited opportunities for students to actively engage in contextual problem-solving related to their daily experiences. This study aims to analyze the effect of the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model assisted by local wisdom-based animated videos on students’ learning motivation and mathematics learning outcomes. This research employed a quasi-experimental design using a posttest-only control group. The population consisted of 235 students, with 64 selected randomly as the sample. Data were collected through a validated learning motivation questionnaire and an essay-type mathematics achievement test. The data were analyzed using Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) to examine both the partial and simultaneous effects of the learning model on the dependent variables. The results revealed that the PBL model assisted by local wisdom-based animated videos significantly improved students’ learning motivation and mathematics learning outcomes, both individually and simultaneously. title: The Effect of a Local Wisdom-Oriented Group Investigation Model Based on Tri Kaya Parisudha on Students’ Cooperation Attitudes and Critical Thinking Skills in Integrated Science and Social Studies
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of the Group Investigation learning model oriented toward local wisdom Tri Kaya Parisudha on students’ cooperation attitudes and critical thinking skills in Elementary School science and social studies subjects. The target population consisted of all elementary school students in Cluster II Santalia Kubutambahan, comprising seven schools, with a sample of 63 students selected randomly. This study employed a quasi-experimental method with a posttest control group design. Data were collected using observation sheets to assess cooperation attitudes and essay tests to measure students’ critical thinking skills. Data analysis was conducted using Multivariate Analysis of Variance. title: Application of Quizizz Learning Media on Senior High School Students' Learning Outcomes Based on Learning Styles
abstract: The study was motivated by the low geography learning outcomes of students, which were attributed to the lack of variety in learning media and the suboptimal implementation of learning styles. The purpose of this study was to analyze the effect of using Quizizz as a learning medium on high school students’ geography learning outcomes based on their learning styles. The research employed a quasi-experimental method with a nonequivalent control group design. Data were collected through questionnaires, observations, tests, and documentation. The results showed that the use of Quizizz significantly improved students’ learning outcomes, particularly by accommodating different learning styles. Quizizz supports various learning styles through its features, such as visual learners benefiting from engaging visuals and multiple-choice, short-answer, and essay options; kinesthetic learners being supported by drawing-answer features or using paper mode during quizzes; and auditory learners being facilitated through audio and video features for delivering questions and answers. The study concludes that Quizizz significantly enhances geography learning outcomes compared to classes that do not us

title: Role-Playing-Based Civics Education as an Effort to Improve Interfaith Tolerance Attitudes
abstract: The low effectiveness of Civic Education (PKN) learning in instilling an attitude of tolerance between religious communities among elementary school students is the background of this study. The still dominant use of conventional learning methods that only focus on cognitive aspects causes character values such as tolerance to be less optimally internalized. This study aims to determine the effectiveness of the role play-based PKN learning model in increasing the attitude of tolerance between religions in grade III students. This study uses the Classroom Action Research (PTK) method with a qualitative and quantitative descriptive approach. The subjects in this study were 24 students. The data collection technique was carried out through tolerance attitude questionnaires given before and after treatment (pre-test and post-test), observation of student activities during learning, and student reflection journals. The data obtained were analyzed statistically descriptive to describe the spread and increase of tolerance attitudes, and qualitatively analyzed to describe students' affective responses to the learning process. title: Traditional Games and Body Mass Index in Improving Children's Motor Skills: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Motoric skills and physical activity are fundamental elements in the holistic development of children. However, the decline in motor capacity and the increasing prevalence of obesity have become significant challenges during early childhood development. This condition is exacerbated by low levels of physical activity, largely influenced by the dominance of gadget use and a sedentary lifestyle among children. This study aims to analyze and synthesize empirical evidence regarding the influence of traditional games and body mass index on the enhancement of children’s motor abilities. The study adopts a systematic review design guided by the PRISMA 2020 protocol, employing the PICOS framework for inclusion criteria determination and the SALSA approach for literature synthesis. A total of 14 eligible scientific articles were qualitatively analyzed. title: The Impact of Implementing the Discovery Learning Model on Improving Civics Learning Outcomes
abstract: In the learning process of Civic Education (PKn), not all teachers have applied an approach centered on student activity. The role of teachers as facilitators has not been carried out optimally, because most teachers still rely on lecture and question and answer methods as the main learning strategy. The purpose of this study is to analyze the impact of the application of the discovery learning model in improving the learning outcomes of PPKn. This study uses a quasi-experimental method, taking samples using a simple random sampling technique. The research sample as an experimental class was 34 students and a total control class of 35 students. The techniques and data collection instruments in this study are student learning outcome tests, observation, and documentation. The results of the study showed the results of the hypothesis test using the Independent Sample T-Test conducted through IBM SPSS Statistics software version 22, which found that there was a significant difference between the results of the posttest of students in the experimental class and the control class. title: Civics Learning through the Use of Regional Children’s Songs in Fostering a Sense of Patriotism among First Grade Elementary School Students
abstract: Instilling a sense of patriotism in elementary school students often faces challenges, particularly due to children’s limited understanding of abstract concepts such as nationalism and patriotism. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of Citizenship Education (PKN) learning using traditional children’s songs in fostering patriotism among first-grade students. The research employed a One-Shot Case Study design with a sample of 24 students. The learning was designed using traditional children’s songs as a medium that contains national values, with the expectation of strengthening students’ understanding and attitudes toward nationalism from an early age. Data were collected through a post-test measuring patriotic attitudes and student activity observation sheets validated by experts. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics and a one-sample t-test with the assistance of SPSS software. title: Problem-Based Learning-Based Civics Education as an Effort to Increase the Awareness of Fourth Grade Students
abstract: The low social concern of elementary school students is caused by the learning of Civic Education (PKn) which is still conventional, teacher-centered, and minimal active student involvement. The purpose of this study is to describe and analyze the application of the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model in improving social awareness of grade IV elementary school students. The research subjects consist of grade IV elementary school students who are actively involved in problem-based PKn learning. The research method used is a descriptive quantitative approach with a One-Shot Case Study design. Data was collected through social awareness questionnaires and student behavior observation sheets during the learning process. The data analysis technique was carried out descriptively by examining students' social behavior tendencies, which included empathy, cooperation, participation in group activities, initiative to help friends, and responsibility for tasks. The results of the study show that the application of the PBL model has a positive impact on increasing students' social awareness. title: Project-Based Learning Assisted by Virtual Practicals with the PhET Application as an Effort to Improve Scientific Attitudes and Literacy
abstract: Learning science in elementary schools still faces various challenges, particularly the low levels of students’ scientific attitudes and scientific literacy due to limited practicum facilities, the dominance of lecture-based teaching, and the lack of opportunities for independent exploration and investigation. These conditions reduce student engagement, curiosity, and their ability to understand and apply scientific concepts in daily life. Based on these issues, this study aims to analyze the effect of the Project Based Learning model supported by virtual practicum using the PhET application on improving elementary students’ scientific attitudes and scientific literacy. This research employed a quantitative method with a quasi-experimental Nonequivalent Pretest–Posttest Control Group Design involving two groups: an experimental group that received PjBL supported by PhET simulations and a control group that received conventional instruction. The research subjects consisted of 62 fourth-grade students selected using saturated sampling. title: APOS Theory-Based Learning on the Procedural Fluency of Fourth-Grade Elementary School Students
abstract: Procedural fluency represents an essential ability that reflects students’ skills in executing systematic steps to solve problems efficiently, particularly in mathematics learning, which is often perceived as challenging by elementary school students. In reality, many students still struggle to understand mathematical problem-solving procedures in a coherent and flexible manner, resulting in learning that tends to emphasize memorizing steps rather than developing deep conceptual understanding. This condition highlights the need for a learning model that can integrate conceptual understanding with procedural skills in a balanced way. This study aims to examine the effect of APOS Theory-Based Learning on improving the procedural fluency of elementary school students. The research employed a quasi-experimental method using a Non-Equivalent Post-Test Only Control Group Design. The subjects consisted of elementary school students divided into experimental and control groups through a cluster random sampling technique. title: Management Quality of Education and Training in Increasing the Capacity of Lecturer at Seskoad Bandung
abstract: The quality management of education and training (Diklat) plays a strategic role in enhancing the capacity of lecturers at Sesko AD Bandung. This study is motivated by the need to develop teaching quality and lecturer competencies to support the achievement of military higher education objectives. The study aims to analyze the effectiveness of quality management in Diklat programs and identify factors that facilitate or hinder the enhancement of lecturer capacity. The research employed a qualitative approach, with data collected through observation, interviews, and document analysis. Data analysis was conducted descriptively to illustrate the implementation of quality management in Diklat. The results indicate that the application of quality management in Diklat at Sesko AD Bandung has had a positive impact on improving lecturer competencies, particularly in pedagogical skills, teaching methodology, and understanding of curricula based on strategic needs.
